name: Monorepo-Bench
intro: Monorepo-Bench 是 GPT-5.3-Codex 系统卡披露的 OpenAI 内部大型仓库软件与研究工程评测。每个样本从改动前分支开始，由智能体按人工编写、描述所需改动的拉取请求式提示修改代码；系统卡另称线索由人工编写，但未披露是否或如何向智能体提供。全部任务专用隐藏测试通过才记为成功，Figure 8 以 pass@1 报告结果。
build_method: 内部大型仓库, 人工编写改动提示、线索与隐藏单元测试（线索投喂方式未披露）
metric: Pass@1（全部任务专用隐藏测试必须通过）
task_type: 软件工程, 大型仓库任务
eval_feature: 改动前分支, 人工改动提示, 线索投喂未披露, CLI 与 Python 智能体运行, 全隐藏测试通过门槛, pass@1
build_method_en: Internal Large Repository, Human-written Change Prompts, Hints, and Hidden Unit Tests (Hint Delivery Undisclosed)
eval_feature_en: Pre-change Branch, Human-written Change Prompt, Hint Delivery Undisclosed, CLI/Python Agentic Rollout, All-hidden-tests-pass Gate, Pass@1
intro_en: Monorepo-Bench is OpenAI's in-house large-repository software- and research-engineering evaluation disclosed in the GPT-5.3-Codex system card. Each sample starts from a pre-change branch and asks an agent to modify code from a human-written pull-request-style prompt describing the required changes. The card also says hints are human-written but does not disclose whether or how they are supplied to the agent. Success requires every task-specific hidden test to pass, and Figure 8 reports pass@1.
metric_en: Pass@1 (all task-specific hidden tests must pass)

drawio_review_note: Primary-source audit completed 2026-07-21 against the official GPT-5.3-Codex System Card dated February 5, 2026, using the current official PDF at https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-3-codex/gpt-5-3-codex.pdf with SHA-256 320635949a1e8b127af026167c4e991bb73a7e1f2ab824ee07fd764a92708107. Table 6 places Monorepo-Bench in AI Self-Improvement and describes its capability as real-world software-engineering and research-engineering tasks. The disclosed objective is to measure whether models can replicate pull-request-style contributions in a large internal repository, graded by hidden tests. Section 5.1.3.1 defines one evaluation sample as one agentic rollout and gives exactly three protocol steps: the agent's code environment is checked out to a pre-change branch and receives a prompt describing required changes; the agent uses command-line tools and Python to modify files within the codebase; and the completed modifications are graded by a hidden unit test. The following sentence resolves the sample outcome: if all task-specific tests pass, the rollout is considered a success. It also states that prompts, unit tests, and hints are human-written, but does not say whether or how hints are supplied to the agent. The diagram preserves those disclosed facts and does not broaden them into a public SWE-bench-style container contract, repository reset algorithm, dependency installation procedure, patch format, or test parser. Figure 8 explicitly labels the vertical axis pass@1, correcting the prior catalog note that said a pass@1 label would be invented. Direct visual inspection of the official PDF fixes the plotted values at GPT-5.1-Codex-Max 53%, GPT-5.2-Thinking no browse 55%, GPT-5.2-Codex 55%, and GPT-5.3-Codex 56%; the accompanying text says GPT-5.3-Codex performs close to GPT-5.2-Codex and GPT-5.2 Thinking. The chart includes error bars, but the card does not define their statistic or confidence level. The sample-level outcome is binary under the all-task-specific-tests gate: a rollout with every check passing is successful, while a rollout with at least one non-passing check is not successful. The card does not describe partial credit, a secondary score, parser recovery, infrastructure-error treatment, excluded runs, or any retry policy, so none is inferred. The system card does not disclose the benchmark's task count, task list, selection funnel, source pull requests, repository identity, source/target commits, task weighting, hidden-test counts, human author or reviewer counts, acceptance rate, deduplication, contamination checks, split, rollout budget, token or turn limit, stop rule beyond completion, model generation parameters, temperature, reasoning effort, compaction, browser or network access, sandbox details, package installation, or error-bar computation. Details from the preceding Irregular cybersecurity evaluation—such as xhigh reasoning, web search, autonomous sandbox bypass, 1,000 turns, or compaction—are section-local and are not transferred into Monorepo-Bench. The benchmark is in-house: no public repository, dataset, task artifacts, prompts, hints, unit tests, data license, evaluation harness, submission service, or public leaderboard is linked by the system card or official page. The public evidence boundary is therefore the system-card prose and Figure 8 only. The catalog keeps scale as not disclosed, openness as in-house, and has_leaderboard false.
